items.name: Somnath Jyotirlinga
items.heroSubtitle: The Eternal Abode of Lord Shiva
items.heroText: Seek the blessings of Lord Somnath, the first Jyotirlinga and a symbol of faith, resilience and eternal divinity.
items.heroImageAlt: Somnath Temple on the sea shore at sunset
items.aboutText1: Somnath Jyotirlinga, located in Prabhas Patan, Gujarat, is the first among the twelve Jyotirlingas and holds a special place in Hindu tradition. It is believed to be the sacred abode where Lord Shiva appeared as an infinite pillar of light, representing the beginning and end of all creation.
items.aboutText2: This ancient temple has witnessed the rise and fall of many kingdoms, yet it continues to stand as a symbol of unwavering faith and devotion. Devotees from across the world visit Somnath to seek the blessings of Lord Shiva for strength, peace and prosperity. The divine energy of this temple is associated with renewal, hope and the power to overcome life’s challenges.

items.name: Vaidyanath Jyotirlinga
items.heroSubtitle: The Divine Healer of Lord Shiva
items.heroText: Seek the blessings of Lord Vaidyanath, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, and experience divine healing, protection and spiritual well-being at this sacred temple.
items.aboutText1: Vaidyanath Jyotirlinga, also known as Baidyanath Dham, is a revered shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in Deoghar, Jharkhand. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and holds great significance in Hindu tradition. Lord Shiva is worshipped here as the Divine Healer (Vaidya), who removes suffering, cures ailments and blesses devotees with good health and long life.

items.name: Rameshwaram Jyotirlinga
items.heroText: Explore the divine Rameshwaram Jyotirlinga, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, and experience the spiritual connection of Lord Shiva and Lord Rama at this sacred temple.
items.aboutText1: Rameshwaram Jyotirlinga is a revered shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, located in Rameshwaram, Tamil Nadu. It is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and holds great religious significance in Hindu tradition. The temple is associated with Lord Rama, who is believed to have worshipped Lord Shiva here before crossing the sea to Lanka.
items.aboutText2: The Ramanathaswamy Temple is famous for its magnificent Dravidian architecture, longest temple corridor in India and 22 sacred wells (theerthams) within the temple premises. Devotees visit Rameshwaram to seek blessings, perform rituals and experience the deep spiritual energy of this holy place.
